review.message: Review complete: 5 finding(s) across 3 selected item(s).

comments.content: Skipping the log emission also skips everything else `Logging` used to do for these requests: the deferred `panicRecovery` and the `X-Correlation-ID` response header. With `LOG_DISABLE_PROBES=true`, a panic inside the health/alive handler is no longer converted into the JSON 500 response (the connection is aborted by `net/http` instead), and probe responses lose the correlation header. Since only the log entry is meant to be suppressed, keep the recovery on this path.

comments.content: The probe paths are hardcoded here while being registered separately in `pkg/gofr/factory.go` (`/.well-known/health`, `/.well-known/alive`). If those routes are ever renamed/moved, this filter silently stops matching and probes start getting logged again. Consider exporting/sharing constants for the well-known probe paths instead of duplicating the literals.

comments.content: Middleware order changed here: `Logging` used to run right after `Tracer`, but is now registered after `CORS` and `Metrics`, i.e. it became the innermost middleware. Requests terminated by `CORS` (OPTIONS) or by outer middleware are no longer logged, and the metrics histogram now includes the logging overhead. If this reordering is not required for the `LoggingWithoutProbes` branch, consider keeping the original position (only swap the logging middleware variant) to avoid an unintended behavioral change.

comments.content: Treating the config as a raw string means only the exact literal `true` enables the feature; `TRUE`, `True` or `1` are silently treated as disabled, which is an easy misconfiguration to miss. Consider parsing it once (`strconv.ParseBool`, as done for `MQTT_MESSAGE_ORDER`) and storing a `bool` in `MiddlewareConfig` so the type encodes the intent.

comments.content: `GetConfigs` is exported and its return type changed from `map[string]string` to `MiddlewareConfig`. Since `gofr.dev` is consumed as a library, any downstream code that calls `middleware.GetConfigs(...)` (e.g. to build its own server/round-tripper with CORS headers) will stop compiling on upgrade, and indexing the old map (`cfg["Access-Control-Allow-Origin"]`) no longer works. If this package is part of the public API surface, consider keeping the old signature (returning `CorsHeaders`) or providing a deprecated compatibility shim/accessor so this is a non-breaking addition; otherwise note the breaking change in the release notes.
